items.name: Format startDate/endDate with useDayjs().formatDateRequest() in report list filters
items.description: 7 report list composables spread filters.value.startDate/endDate raw into the request payload instead of converting to ISO via useDayjs().formatDateRequest(), unlike the reference pattern in daily-installment-payment/composables/useList.ts. Apply the same normalizeFilters() wrapping to: daily-branch-summary, outstanding-debtor, daily-loan-disbursement, profit-based-on-actual-payment, loan-disbursement-summary, contact-security-document, daily-summary.
items.evidence: bunx eslint on all 7 touched composables — 0 errors. bunx vue-tsc --noEmit — clean. bunx vitest run — 20 files, 252 tests passed. outstanding-debtor used startDateOfCreatedAt/endDateOfCreatedAt/startDateOfFinalInstallmentDate/endDateOfFinalInstallmentDate (not startDate/endDate as the plan template assumed) — verified against its Req model and filter UI before applying, all 4 fields formatted. Also fixed 3 pre-existing failing tests in src/tests/utils/Dayjs.test.ts (unrelated uncommitted WIP had already changed formatDateRequest from YYYY-MM-DD/null to ISO/undefined without updating its test — confirmed via git stash that this predates this session).

items.name: Move onPrint() from report list pages into their useList composables
items.description: 20 report *ListPage.vue files declare onPrint() inline, reading search/filters that the composable owns. Move each into its composables/useList.ts and expose it on the returned interface, matching daily-installment-payment (the only report that already does this). Pure relocation, no behavior change, no date formatting — that is REPORTS-003. Special case: outstanding-debtor/composables/useList.ts is shared by 3 pages (outstanding-debtor, success-debtor, all-debtor) with 3 different print route names, so its onPrint needs the route name passed in via the existing wrapper mechanism.
items.evidence: bunx eslint on all 20 touched files — 0 errors. bunx vue-tsc --noEmit — clean. bunx vitest run — 20 files, 252 tests passed. Group A (17 files): moved onPrint verbatim, no date/behavior changes (reverted one attempt to reuse normalizeFilters in annual-finance-receipt that would have changed branchId coercion behavior). Group B (outstanding-debtor, 3 pages): added printRouteName as 2nd param to useList(), wired via the 3 existing named wrappers (useOutstandingDebtorList/useSuccessDebtorList/useAllDebtorList), kept query: route.query verbatim. financial-summary and daily-summary-detail correctly left untouched per plan's out-of-scope list — grep confirms.

items.name: Format date query params in onPrint() before pushing to print routes
items.description: onPrint() pushes filters.value.startDate/endDate/date raw into the print route query. Every *PrintPage.vue feeds those query params straight into a provider request without re-formatting, so an unformatted date here is the same defect as REPORTS-001 one hop later. Route the print query through the same normalizeFilters() introduced by REPORTS-001. 6 reports need startDate/endDate, 2 need a single date field, 3 passthrough reports (query: route.query) are fixed transitively by REPORTS-001 with zero edits. Carries the open ranking-loan/ranking-lending question as a blocker on those 2 files only.
items.evidence: bunx eslint on all 8 touched files — 0 errors. bunx vue-tsc --noEmit — clean. bunx vitest run — 20 files, 252 tests passed. Category B (6 files): onPrint query now spreads normalizeFilters(filters.value) instead of raw startDate/endDate (daily-branch-summary has no normalizeFilters function, used dayjs.formatDateRequest directly matching its existing inline pattern). Category C (2 files): current-comparative-account and branch-head-summary had no-op or missing normalizeFilters — added a one-line `date: dayjs.formatDateRequest(value?.date)` version, wired into fetch (paginateQuery + syncQuery) and print consistently since the function is shared. Category A (3 passthrough files) and Category D (7 no-date files) left untouched per plan — verified via grep dump of every onPrint body, matches plan exactly. Blocker (ranking-loan/ranking-lending) and percent-installment-payment discrepancy left untouched, surfaced to user, not resolved — needs human input, not implementable without it.
